Respond with your complete implementation plan as a markdown document. Do NOT attempt to read files or check folder structures. Write your full plan directly in your response.

# Codex Peer Review Prompt Paste this entire file into Codex in VS Code. --- ## Your task You are doing an independent architectural peer review. Read the brief below, then produce your own implementation plan. Save your plan as `codex-plan.md` in this folder: `output/sessions/codex-peer-review/2026-04-13_clone-css-rendering-fix/` When done, output this exact command so the user can copy-paste it into Claude Code: ``` /plan.with.codex synthesise output/sessions/codex-peer-review/2026-04-13_clone-css-rendering-fix/ ``` --- ## Brief: Clone CSS Rendering Fix **Date:** 2026-04-13 **Project:** Local Business Platform monorepo (Next.js 15, Turborepo, pnpm workspaces, Tailwind CSS) **Note:** This brief is sent to both Claude and Codex independently. Your plans will be synthesised into a final implementation spec. Do not look at `claude-plan.md` before writing your own plan. ### Problem Statement The platform has a clone-to-theme pipeline that clones live websites (e.g. colorcode.events, a WordPress/Breakdance site), converts the HTML to React JSX components, and produces a theme package for the platform. The pipeline has three stages: 1. **Clone** — wget + Breakdance HTML to JSX converter. Produces high-fidelity clone files. 2. **Extract/Componentize** — Takes clone JSX, extracts header/footer, writes theme page components preserving the original markup. 3. **Strip** — Replaces business-specific content (names, phone numbers, text) with React props to create a reusable template. Stages 1-3 work correctly. The problem is **rendering the componentized theme in a Next.js site**. The clone JSX uses Breakdance CSS classes (`bde-section-17-100`, `bde-div-18-109`, `.breakdance`, `.callout`, `.graphic`, etc.) whose rules exist in 53 downloaded CSS files. Getting this CSS to load in the Next.js/Tailwind pipeline has failed every way tried so far: **Failed attempts:** 1. Concatenating all 53 CSS files into theme `globals.css` — Turbopack's CSS parser rejects complex selectors, inline SVG data URIs, and minified mega-lines in several files (`rsvp.css`, `square.css`) 2. Filtering to 26 essential Breakdance files — `global-settings.css` has `url(icons/eye.svg)` relative path that Turbopack tries to resolve as a module import 3. `@import "../theme-system/dist/base.css"` generated by extract-theme — this file does not exist (working themes don't use this import at all) 4. Removing `@tailwind base;` and `@tailwind components;` from site globals.css — still no layout rendered 5. The `@tailwind base` Preflight reset conflicts with Breakdance's typography, heading sizes, body colors, and layout (Breakdance uses `!important` heavily and expects to be the only CSS framework) **Root causes:** - Breakdance CSS was designed for WordPress, not Next.js/Tailwind - Turbopack is stricter than browsers — rejects syntax browsers accept - PostCSS/Tailwind processes globals.css and may transform or strip non-Tailwind CSS - Breakdance CSS references assets via relative paths (`url(icons/eye.svg)`) that don't exist in the Next.js project - Breakdance loads custom fonts (Aeonik) via `@font-face` with font files that don't exist in Next.js - Breakdance CSS variables (`--bde-section-width`, `--bde-column-gap`) are defined in the very file Turbopack rejects ### Goals 1. Clone CSS renders correctly in a Next.js dev server and production build 2. Clone CSS and Tailwind theme tokens coexist — clone CSS handles layout/visual fidelity, Tailwind handles white-label customization 3. The solution is generic — works for any cloned site, not just corvus/colorcode.events 4. The solution integrates into the existing extract-theme pipeline (automated, not manual per-site) 5. Font loading is handled (either clone fonts or graceful fallback) 6. Images from the clone render correctly ### Non-Goals - Converting Breakdance classes to Tailwind classes (too complex, too brittle) - Supporting every WordPress plugin's CSS (only the layout/visual CSS that affects rendering) - Making clone CSS editable via theme tokens (clone CSS is frozen from the reference site) - Modifying the clone stage (wget + converter) — that works fine - Modifying the strip pass (content-stripper.ts) — that works fine ### Acceptance Criteria 1. `npx next dev` on the corvus test site (`sites/_corvus-digital-marketing-events/`) renders the homepage with visual fidelity to `output/clones/corvus/html/pages/home.html` opened in a browser 2. `npx next build` succeeds without CSS parser errors 3. `pnpm type-check` passes 4. Tailwind utility classes (`bg-brand-primary`, `text-h1`, etc.) still work in the site alongside clone CSS 5. The extract-theme tool handles CSS preprocessing automatically (no manual steps) 6. Images referenced in clone JSX display correctly 7. Custom fonts either load or gracefully degrade ### Constraints **Architecture constraints (from CLAUDE.md):** - Production builds use `next build --webpack` (Turbopack has PostCSS bugs in CI). Turbopack is used for `next dev`. - Never use CSS `theme()` function in plain CSS files — causes CSS parser panics. Use `var(--custom-property)` instead. - Never use `packages/themes/**/*.{ext}` glob patterns — causes 18+ minute builds via node_modules descent. - Theme package filenames: `components/` uses lowercase (`header.tsx`), `pages/` uses PascalCase (`HomePage.tsx`). - Theme `index.ts` must NOT re-export from `./components` or `./pages` (jiti can't resolve them). - Site `vercel.json` must NOT set `outputDirectory`. - Named exports only (no default exports). **CSS/styling constraints:** - Always use theme tokens for white-label styling (`bg-brand-primary`, not hardcoded hex) - No inline styles, no CSS-in-JS — Tailwind only for the platform layer - Clone CSS is an exception — it's frozen/external CSS that provides the visual skeleton **Pipeline constraints:** - Do NOT modify `clone-site.ts`, `scaffold-client-site.ts`, `visual-qa-loop.ts`, or `cpf-validator.ts` - Do NOT modify live site themes (orion, vega, cygnus, solaris) — only corvus - The solution must be automated inside `extract-theme.ts` (or a new helper it calls) ### Relevant Architecture **How working themes load CSS (orion/vega pattern):** ```css /* packages/themes/orion/globals.css */ @import "../../core-components/src/styles/animations.css"; .btn-primary { @apply bg-brand-primary text-white ... } .section { @apply py-16 ... } /* Component classes using @apply + Tailwind tokens */ ``` ```css /* sites/dj-fox-electrical/app/globals.css */ @import "../../../packages/themes/orion/globals.css"; @tailwind base; @tailwind components; @tailwind utilities; @layer base { ... site-specific overrides ... } ``` The theme `globals.css` contains `@apply`-based component classes (Tailwind-native). The site `globals.css` imports it, then declares `@tailwind base/components/utilities`. Tailwind's PostCSS plugin processes everything together. **How clone CSS is different:** The clone `globals.css` contains raw Breakdance CSS (not `@apply`, not Tailwind-aware). It's ~370KB of concatenated WordPress CSS with Breakdance-specific selectors, CSS variables, and font references. This CSS must bypass PostCSS/Tailwind processing entirely. **Current extract-theme.ts `generateGlobalsCss()` function:** ```typescript function generateGlobalsCss(customProperties: string, cloneCss: string): string { return `/* Auto-generated ... */\n@import "../theme-system/dist/base.css";\n\n:root {\n${customProperties}\n}\n\n.container { ... }\n\n/* Clone styles */\n${cloneCss}`; } ``` The `@import "../theme-system/dist/base.css"` is wrong — this file doesn't exist. Working themes import `../../core-components/src/styles/animations.css`. **Clone CSS file inventory (53 files in `output/clones/corvus/assets/css/`):** | Category | Files | Notes | |----------|-------|-------| | Breakdance core layout | `post-13-defaults.css`, `common-full.css`, `common-responsive.css` | Essential — defines `.bde-section`, `.bde-columns`, `.bde-div` layout rules | | Page-specific Breakdance | `post-13.css`, `post-167.css`, `post-3074.css`, etc. | Per-page overrides — needed for visual fidelity | | Global settings | `global-settings.css` | Contains `--bde-section-width`, `--bde-column-gap` variables + problematic `url(icons/eye.svg)` | | Breakdance presets | `presets.css` | Button/typography presets | | WordPress plugins | `rsvp.css`, `square.css`, `free.css`, `style.min.css` | Events Calendar, WooCommerce, etc. — likely not needed | | Fonts | `custom_font_aeonik.css` | `@font-face` for Aeonik — font files don't exist in Next.js | | WordPress core | `normalize.min.css`, `style.min.css` | CSS reset/normalize | **Clone JSX format (from `output/clones/corvus/jsx/pages/HomePage.tsx`):** ```jsx // Extracted inline styles: // :root{--wp--preset--aspect-ratio--square: 1; ...} // .breakdance .bde-section { ... } // ... hundreds of CSS rules as comments ... export function homePage() { return ( <>
...
A Fresh Digital... ``` The extract-theme tool splits at `export function`, treats lines before as CSS (strips `//` comment markers), and uses the JSX body as the component markup. ### Codebase Snapshot | What | Path | Purpose | |------|------|---------| | Extract theme tool | `tools/extract-theme.ts` | Main pipeline tool — generates theme packages from clones | | Content stripper | `tools/lib/content-stripper.ts` | Replaces business content with props | | Clone CSS files | `output/clones/corvus/assets/css/` | 53 downloaded CSS files from colorcode.events | | Clone JSX pages | `output/clones/corvus/jsx/pages/` | Converted HTML-to-JSX components | | Clone images | `output/clones/corvus/assets/images/` | 91 image files | | Corvus theme (WIP) | `packages/themes/corvus/` | Theme package being generated | | Corvus test site | `sites/_corvus-digital-marketing-events/` | Test site (prefixed with `_` to exclude from CI) | | Working theme example | `packages/themes/orion/` | Reference for correct theme structure | | Working site example | `sites/dj-fox-electrical/` | Reference for correct site wiring | | Theme system types | `packages/theme-system/src/types.ts` | Theme config + registry types | | Rendering blockers doc | `output/sessions/2026-04-13_extract-improvements-and-reset/clone-rendering-blockers.md` | Full problem analysis | ### What a Good Plan Should Cover 1. **CSS loading strategy** — How does the clone CSS get into the Next.js page?
